# Spec: a command's short help must not stop at an abbreviation

## Context

When a command has no explicit `short_help`, Click derives one from its help text, for the list of commands shown
by a group's `--help` (`Command.get_short_help_str()` in `src/click/core.py`, which calls
`_make_default_short_help(help, max_length)` in `src/click/utils.py`). The rule today: take the first paragraph,
collapse whitespace, stop at the first word that ends with a period (the end of the first sentence), and truncate
with `...` if the result is longer than `max_length` (45 by default in that call path).

Any word ending with a period is taken as the end of the sentence, so an abbreviation cuts the short help:

```python
@cli.command()
def weigh():
    """Weigh apples vs. pears."""
```

is listed as `weigh  Weigh apples vs.` instead of `weigh  Weigh apples vs. pears.`; the same happens with `e.g.`,
`i.e.`, `etc.` followed by more words.

The tests of the function are in `tests/test_utils/test_make_default_short_help.py`.

## Goal

The first sentence ends at a period only when that period really ends a sentence, and the short help keeps the
rest of its current rules.

## Functional requirements

FR1. In the first paragraph, after whitespace is collapsed, a word that ends with `.` ends the first sentence only
if it is the last word of the paragraph, or the next word does not start with a lowercase character (as defined by
Python's `str.islower()` on that first character). Otherwise the period belongs to an abbreviation and the sentence
goes on. So `"Weigh apples vs. pears."` is one sentence; `"Pick a fruit. 3 remain."` ends after `fruit.`;
`"Read e.g. the docs. Then go."` ends after `docs.`.

FR2. The short help is the first sentence (or the whole first paragraph if no word ends a sentence). If it is not
longer than `max_length`, it is returned as it is.

FR3. Otherwise it is truncated: as many whole leading words as fit, joined by single spaces, immediately followed
by `...`, so that the total length is at most `max_length`. A word is never split, hyphenated words included. If not
even the first word fits with the `...`, the result is `...`.

FR4. Narrow widths: if `max_length` is smaller than 3 (zero and negative values included) and the text does not
fit, the result is `...` (the only case where the result may be longer than `max_length`). A text that fits is
still returned as it is (`"ab"` with `max_length` 2 gives `"ab"`).

FR5. Unchanged: only the first paragraph is considered (text up to the first blank line); a leading `\b` no-rewrap
marker is ignored; empty help gives `""`; a period inside a word (`~/.netrc`) is not a sentence end.

FR6. The existing test case that relies on the old rule (`"123 567 9. aaaa bbb"` with width 10, which today gives
`"123 567 9."`) is updated to the new rule (`"123 567..."`, since `aaaa` is lowercase), and new cases cover FR1 to
FR5. An end-to-end test checks the command list of a group's `--help`.

FR7. `CHANGES.md` gains an entry in the unreleased section at the top describing the change.

## Codebase areas involved (indicative)

- `src/click/utils.py`: `_make_default_short_help`.
- `src/click/core.py`: `Command.get_short_help_str` (caller, unchanged).
- `tests/test_utils/test_make_default_short_help.py`.
- `CHANGES.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

AC1. `_make_default_short_help("Weigh apples vs. pears.", 30) == "Weigh apples vs. pears."` and
`_make_default_short_help("Weigh apples vs. pears and plums.", 20) == "Weigh apples vs...."`.

AC2. Every example of FR1 to FR5 gives the stated result, with and without a leading `\b` marker paragraph.

AC3. The result is never longer than `max(max_length, 3)`.

AC4. A group whose subcommand has the help `"Weigh apples vs. pears."` lists it in `--help` as
`Weigh apples vs. pears.`.

AC5. The whole test suite passes (`python -m pytest`).

## Assumptions

- An abbreviation followed by a capitalised word (`U.S. Army`) is taken as a sentence end: this limit is accepted.

## Out of scope

- The explicit `short_help` argument, the help of options and arguments, the formatting of the help page.
- New dependencies.

**Objective.** `_make_default_short_help` (`src/click/utils.py:62`) stops treating every word ending with a period as a sentence end, and takes the first sentence before it decides on truncation. Signature and privacy unchanged.

**Current behaviour.** One loop measures and looks for the period at once: the first fitting word ending with `.` returns immediately, so `Weigh apples vs. pears.` gives `Weigh apples vs.`.

**D1 — two passes.** The loop becomes two steps, in this order: (1) cut `words` at the first sentence end; (2) join and, if longer than `max_length`, truncate. **D3 — empty after the marker.** The `\b` marker is removed before the empty check: `if words and words[0] == "\b"`, then `if not words: return ""`. # Spec: a command's short help must not stop at an abbreviation

## Context

When a command has no explicit `short_help`, Click derives one from its help text, for the list of commands shown
by a group's `--help` (`Command.get_short_help_str()` in `src/click/core.py`, which calls
`_make_default_short_help(help, max_length)` in `src/click/utils.py`). The rule today: take the first paragraph,
collapse whitespace, stop at the first word that ends with a period (the end of the first sentence), and truncate
with `...` if the result is longer than `max_length` (45 by default in that call path).

Any word ending with a period is taken as the end of the sentence, so an abbreviation cuts the short help:

```python
@cli.command()
def weigh():
    """Weigh apples vs. pears."""
```

is listed as `weigh  Weigh apples vs.` instead of `weigh  Weigh apples vs. pears.`; the same happens with `e.g.`,
`i.e.`, `etc.` followed by more words.

The tests of the function are in `tests/test_utils/test_make_default_short_help.py`.

## Goal

The first sentence ends at a period only when that period really ends a sentence, and the short help keeps the
rest of its current rules.

## Functional requirements

FR1. In the first paragraph, after whitespace is collapsed, a word that ends with `.` ends the first sentence only
if it is the last word of the paragraph, or the next word does not start with a lowercase character (as defined by
Python's `str.islower()` on that first character). Otherwise the period belongs to an abbreviation and the sentence
goes on. So `"Weigh apples vs. pears."` is one sentence; `"Pick a fruit. 3 remain."` ends after `fruit.`;
`"Read e.g. the docs. Then go."` ends after `docs.`.

FR2. The short help is the first sentence (or the whole first paragraph if no word ends a sentence). If it is not
longer than `max_length`, it is returned as it is.

FR3. Otherwise it is truncated: as many whole leading words as fit, joined by single spaces, immediately followed
by `...`, so that the total length is at most `max_length`. A word is never split, hyphenated words included. If not
even the first word fits with the `...`, the result is `...`.

FR4. Narrow widths: if `max_length` is smaller than 3 (zero and negative values included) and the text does not
fit, the result is `...` (the only case where the result may be longer than `max_length`). A text that fits is
still returned as it is (`"ab"` with `max_length` 2 gives `"ab"`).

FR5. Unchanged: only the first paragraph is considered (text up to the first blank line); a leading `\b` no-rewrap
marker is ignored; empty help gives `""`; a period inside a word (`~/.netrc`) is not a sentence end.

FR6. The existing test case that relies on the old rule (`"123 567 9. aaaa bbb"` with width 10, which today gives
`"123 567 9."`) is updated to the new rule (`"123 567..."`, since `aaaa` is lowercase), and new cases cover FR1 to
FR5. An end-to-end test checks the command list of a group's `--help`.

FR7. `CHANGES.md` gains an entry in the unreleased section at the top describing the change.

1	# Spec: a command's short help must not stop at an abbreviation
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	When a command has no explicit `short_help`, Click derives one from its help text, for the list of commands shown
6	by a group's `--help` (`Command.get_short_help_str()` in `src/click/core.py`, which calls
7	`_make_default_short_help(help, max_length)` in `src/click/utils.py`). The rule today: take the first paragraph,
8	collapse whitespace, stop at the first word that ends with a period (the end of the first sentence), and truncate
9	with `...` if the result is longer than `max_length` (45 by default in that call path).
10	
11	Any word ending with a period is taken as the end of the sentence, so an abbreviation cuts the short help:
12	
13	```python
14	@cli.command()
15	def weigh():
16	    """Weigh apples vs. pears."""
17	```
18	
19	is listed as `weigh  Weigh apples vs.` instead of `weigh  Weigh apples vs. pears.`; the same happens with `e.g.`,
20	`i.e.`, `etc.` followed by more words.
21	
22	The tests of the function are in `tests/test_utils/test_make_default_short_help.py`.
23	
24	## Goal
25	
26	The first sentence ends at a period only when that period really ends a sentence, and the short help keeps the
27	rest of its current rules.
28	
29	## Functional requirements
30	
31	FR1. In the first paragraph, after whitespace is collapsed, a word that ends with `.` ends the first sentence only
32	if it is the last word of the paragraph, or the next word does not start with a lowercase character (as defined by
33	Python's `str.islower()` on that first character). Otherwise the period belongs to an abbreviation and the sentence
34	goes on. So `"Weigh apples vs. pears."` is one sentence; `"Pick a fruit. 3 remain."` ends after `fruit.`;
35	`"Read e.g. the docs. Then go."` ends after `docs.`.
36	
37	FR2. The short help is the first sentence (or the whole first paragraph if no word ends a sentence). If it is not
38	longer than `max_length`, it is returned as it is.
39	
40	FR3. Otherwise it is truncated: as many whole leading words as fit, joined by single spaces, immediately followed
41	by `...`, so that the total length is at most `max_length`. A word is never split, hyphenated words included. If not
42	even the first word fits with the `...`, the result is `...`.
43	
44	FR4. Narrow widths: if `max_length` is smaller than 3 (zero and negative values included) and the text does not
45	fit, the result is `...` (the only case where the result may be longer than `max_length`). A text that fits is
46	still returned as it is (`"ab"` with `max_length` 2 gives `"ab"`).
47	
48	FR5. Unchanged: only the first paragraph is considered (text up to the first blank line); a leading `\b` no-rewrap
49	marker is ignored; empty help gives `""`; a period inside a word (`~/.netrc`) is not a sentence end.
50	
51	FR6. The existing test case that relies on the old rule (`"123 567 9. aaaa bbb"` with width 10, which today gives
52	`"123 567 9."`) is updated to the new rule (`"123 567..."`, since `aaaa` is lowercase), and new cases cover FR1 to
53	FR5. An end-to-end test checks the command list of a group's `--help`.
54	
55	FR7. `CHANGES.md` gains an entry in the unreleased section at the top describing the change.
56

60	- `src/click/core.py`: `Command.get_short_help_str` (caller, unchanged).

99	### Decisions
100	**Objective.** `_make_default_short_help` (`src/click/utils.py:62`) stops treating every word ending with a period as a sentence end, and takes the first sentence before it decides on truncation. Signature and privacy unchanged.
101	
102	**Current behaviour.** One loop measures and looks for the period at once: the first fitting word ending with `.` returns immediately, so `Weigh apples vs. pears.` gives `Weigh apples vs.`.
103	
104	**D1 — two passes.** The loop becomes two steps, in this order: (1) cut `words` at the first sentence end; (2) join and, if longer than `max_length`, truncate. The sentence test is exactly `word[-1] == "." and not words[i + 1][0].islower()`, looping over every word but the last, so the last word never needs a test: with no sentence end the whole paragraph is the sentence (FR2). The expression `not words[i + 1][0].islower()` appears once in the file (the T1 mutation searches for it). The first-paragraph cut and `help.split()` stay as they are.
105	
106	**D2 — truncation.** A new forward count replaces the `while i > 0` loop: start from `len("...")`, add each word plus one space after the first word, stop at the first total above `max_length`; the result is the kept words joined by one space, plus `...`. No kept words gives `...`, which also covers every `max_length` below 3 (FR4). The result is never longer than `max(max_length, 3)` (AC3).
107	
108	**D3 — empty after the marker.** The `\b` marker is removed before the empty check: `if words and words[0] == "\b"`, then `if not words: return ""`. Otherwise a marker alone with a negative `max_length` would fail the fit test and return `...` instead of `""` (FR5; today it returns `""`, because the old loop never runs).
109	
110	**D4 — accepted edge cases, literal from FR1.** A next word starting with an uncased character (`(see`, `3`) does not start with a lowercase character, so the period ends the sentence. `U.S. Army` ends at `U.S.` (spec Assumptions).

63	    """Returns a condensed version of help string.
64	
65	    :meta private:
66	    """
67	    # Consider only the first paragraph.
68	    paragraph_end = help.find("\n\n")
69	
70	    if paragraph_end != -1:
71	        help = help[:paragraph_end]
72	
73	    # Collapse newlines, tabs, and spaces.
74	    words = help.split()
75	
76	    # The first paragraph started with a "no rewrap" marker, ignore it.
77	    if words and words[0] == "\b":
78	        words = words[1:]
79	
80	    if not words:
81	        return ""
82	
83	    # A period ends the first sentence only if the next word does not start
84	    # with a lowercase character, otherwise it belongs to an abbreviation.
85	    for i, word in enumerate(words[:-1]):
86	        if word[-1] == "." and not words[i + 1][0].islower():
87	            words = words[: i + 1]
88	            break
89	
90	    text = " ".join(words)
91	
92	    if len(text) <= max_length:
93	        return text
94	
95	    # Keep the whole leading words that fit along with the suffix. The full
96	    # text does not fit, so the loop always stops at the first word to drop.
97	    total_length = len("...")
98	
99	    for i, word in enumerate(words):
100	        total_length += len(word) + (i > 0)
101	
102	        if total_length > max_length:
103	            break
104	
105	    return " ".join(words[:i]) + "..."
